Brandon Sanderson

and recently I've wanted to start reading Discworld stuff. I really enjoy world creation and anything unique and far from the lotr model.
Personally, I'd suggest reading the Discworld city watch series.
I just started reading The Color of Magic last night and it's pretty solid so far. Pratchett is an amazing story teller.

I really enjoy the innocent mage series.

It's 2 duologies and a single book that's a prequel to them, but set way before.

They're written by Karen miller.

I'm currently reading the circle of time series, a monstrous 14 book long epic where each book is about 700 pages. It's really well written though, just takes a lot of time.

The Gormenghast Trilogy! It's low fantasy, sort of treads into sci-fi by the third book. The prose is great, the characters are extremely memorable, and it was definitely one of the best fantasy series I've ever read.

I'm reading VanderMeer's Annihilation right now. Fascinating book, it's fantastical horror, sort of. I'm really bad at defining genres but it's definitely worth reading.

My all-time favourite fantasy series is Chronicles of An Age of Darkness, by Hugh Cook.

It's such an unusual way of arranging a series (the books tend to be set from the perspective of a wildly-varied cast of characters, showing major events in the world from very different viewpoints) and I really love the prose. It's a tragedy that (supposedly) only ten books were released due to its commercial failure- mainly because of the third book. Still, it's a complete, very enjoyable series regardless.

As for "reading now", I sadly haven't been able to sink my teeth into any good medieval fantasies for a while. I'm thinking of giving the Malazan series a go.

I don't think she's super popular, but my favorite author is Hilari Bell. She's done a few more black and white stories, but she usually writes about situations where it's more ambiguous who's right or wrong. And between all her books I can only think of one main character I wasn't wild about.

If you're looking for some intelligent fantasy with strong characters and settings, I recommend Robin Hobb and also the Empire Trilogy.

If you're looking for some old-school fantasy, without weird stuff like the messed-up gender relations in Wheel of Time, you could try Memory, Sorrow, and Thorn.

I'm a big fan of fantasy, but I'm not sure I'm a big fan of the fantasy genre. What I mean is that when I walk into the fantasy section in a book store, I feel like most of the books are basically a D&D campaign written out. These can be fun, and some are really good (Weis and Hickman's Dragonlance books are really good ... well the first 4 are anyway), but not typically my cup of tea. On the other hand, I really love Murakami's books that take place in the "real world" but have a healthy dose of magic in there.

All that being said, my favorite authors are probably Murakami, David Mitchell, and Neil Stephenson. Those are about the only three authors I will read without even glancing at the book. Favorite Book is Cloud Atlas. I'm currently reading Egg and Spoon by Gregory McGuire. It's a fairy tale fantasy novel by the same guy who wrote the Wicked series. So far, it's pretty good.

If you're looking for some stuff that's more classic, check out Roger Zelazny's Chronicles of Amber and the books about Vlad Taltos written by Stephen Brust. Both of these guys deserve more recognition than they get. Zelazny was the mentor to Brust as well as Neil Gaiman, and Gaiman and Brust are still very close.
I highly recommend "The Lies of Locke Lamora" by Scott Lynch. That whole series is brilliant but start with that one. Never see it in these sort of lists.
